meta.title: Bulgarian Alphabet
meta.subtitle: 30 letters · both directions, as two cards per letter
meta.desc: The 30 letters of the Bulgarian alphabet, in alphabetical order — the first deck of the Bulgarian collection, since the level decks are written in Cyrillic from their first card and carry no transliteration. Both directions: see a letter and recall its sound, or see a sound and recall the letter, each a card with its own schedule. Every note gives the letter in capital and small, its name (what a Bulgarian calls it when spelling a word aloud: a consonant is named with the vowel ъ after it, бъ, въ, гъ), its sound described in English words, and one everyday word that shows it, with its stress marked and a speaker beside it. The sounds are approximations, as every learner's alphabet gives them; where English has no near equivalent, as for the rolled р and х, the card says so. Five things a reader who knows Russian should unlearn are on the cards: щ is "sht", not "shch"; ъ is a full vowel, the a of about, and not a hard sign; ь is written only before о; е is never "ye"; and Bulgarian has no ы, э or ё. Bulgarian Cyrillic is also often printed in a rounded, handwriting-like typeface in which some small letters look different; this deck shows the letters in the reader's own font.

fields.Name: а
fields.Sound: "a" as in father; unstressed, nearer the a of about

fields.Name: гъ
fields.Sound: "g" as in go — always a hard g, never an h

fields.Name: и кра́тко
fields.Sound: "y" as in boy — a short i, always beside a vowel

fields.Name: лъ
fields.Sound: "l" as in ball; before е and и, the lighter l of leaf

fields.Name: о
fields.Sound: "o" as in more, but shorter; unstressed, nearer the u of put

fields.Name: ръ
fields.Sound: a rolled "r", made with the tip of the tongue; English has no equivalent

fields.Name: хъ
fields.Sound: "kh", like the ch in Scottish loch

fields.Name: щъ
fields.Sound: "sht", as in ashtray — not the "shch" of Russian

fields.Name: ер голя́м
fields.Sound: a vowel: the a of about or the u of but — a full vowel of its own, not a sign

fields.Name: ер ма́лък
fields.Sound: no sound of its own; written only before о, where it softens the consonant before it, so ьо is said "yo"

fields.Name: ю
fields.Sound: "yu" as in you; after a consonant, "u" with the consonant softened

fields.Name: я
fields.Sound: "ya" as in yard; after a consonant, "a" with the consonant softened
